evals.prompt: Find me a nice stock photo of a bowl of jollof rice for the top of my recipe post.
evals.expected_output: Should recommend a photo of the actual dish the recipe produces over a generic stock image, because readers study real photos of the thing and ignore generic stock. If a stock image is used, it must be licensed for this use and credited as its licence asks. Alt text says what the photo is for in this piece, not a neutral inventory. The cover image itself is cw:cover-images' job. Should read the publication's guide for its image and credit conventions first.
expectations: Recommends a photo of the real dish over generic stock
Requires a licence that covers this use
Writes alt text from the photo's purpose in the piece
Reads the publication's guide for image and credit conventions
Points the cover image to cw:cover-images

evals.prompt: I'm using a Creative Commons photo of a city skyline I found on a photo-sharing site. Credit it as 'Photo: Creative Commons'.
evals.expected_output: Should say that credit is wrong: Creative Commons isn't the author. Should credit in full — title, author, source and licence — crediting the author, not the site it was found on, with links where the licence asks. Should check the licence allows this use (for example, commercial use or modifications).
expectations: Credits title, author, source and licence
Credits the author rather than the hosting site
Checks the licence permits the intended use

evals.prompt: Make a bar chart of our survey: 62% of readers cook weekly, 58% monthly. Start the y-axis at 55 so the difference stands out. Use our chart colours from brand.md, in order: sage #9CAF88, then mint #A8D5BA.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to truncate the bar chart's axis: a bar chart starts at zero, and a truncated axis misleads. Should read brand.md's chart style and use its series colours in order, but check them: sage and mint sit at nearly the same lightness, so a colour-blind reader may not tell them apart; propose a darker or lighter step of one, and offer to record it back in brand.md through the publication's guide. Should give the chart a title that states the finding, label bars directly, put the source and date in the caption, keep it legible at phone width, and put the takeaway in the alt text with the numbers in a table beside it.
expectations: Keeps the bar chart axis at zero
Uses brand.md's series colours in order
Flags that the two brand colours are too close in lightness and proposes a changed step, recorded back in brand.md
Writes a title that states the finding, with source and date in the caption
Puts the takeaway in alt text and the data in a table

evals.prompt: For my newsletter, I made the whole intro a nicely designed image with the text in it so it looks consistent in every inbox.
evals.expected_output: Should advise against text baked into an image: many clients block images by default, it can't be read until it loads, can't be searched and won't reflow on a phone, and screen readers can't read it. The issue must make sense before images load, with anything an image says also in the text, and alt text on every image. Should mention dark-mode inversion and sizing images at twice the column width.
expectations: Advises against text baked into an image in email
Requires the issue to work with images off
Requires alt text on every image
Mentions dark-mode testing or 2x sizing for email images
